The Great Depression & World War II

cards.title: The First Americans Arrive
cards.description: The first people reached North America by crossing a land bridge called Beringia.

cards.title: The Bering Land Bridge
cards.description: The land bridge connected Asia to modern-day Alaska during the Ice Age.

cards.title: Nomadic Hunters
cards.description: These early people were nomads who moved constantly to hunt animals.

cards.title: Filling Two Continents
cards.description: Over many generations, these groups spread south all the way to South America.

cards.title: Hundreds of Different Cultures
cards.description: Diverse civilizations developed, each adapting uniquely to its environment.

cards.title: Ancestral Puebloans
cards.description: The Ancestral Puebloans built remarkable cliff dwellings in the Southwest.

cards.title: The Mississippians & Cahokia
cards.description: The Mississippians built giant earthen mounds, like the great city of Cahokia.

cards.title: The Iroquois Confederacy
cards.description: The Iroquois formed a powerful alliance that united five nations in peace.

cards.title: The Three Sisters
cards.description: Native farmers grew corn, beans, and squash together as “The Three Sisters.”

cards.title: The Inuit of the Arctic
cards.description: The Inuit adapted to the freezing temperatures of the far northern Arctic.

cards.title: The Plains Nations & the Bison
cards.description: Plains tribes like the Sioux relied heavily on the American bison.

cards.title: Oral Tradition
cards.description: Native Americans used storytelling to pass down history, laws, and beliefs.

cards.title: Leif Erikson Reaches America
cards.description: Around the year 1000, the Norse explorer Leif Erikson reached North America.

cards.title: The Viking Settlement of Vinland
cards.description: The Vikings called their short-lived North American settlement “Vinland.”

cards.title: Columbus Sails West
cards.description: Sailing for Spain, Christopher Columbus crossed the Atlantic in 1492 looking for Asia.

cards.title: Mistaken for the “Indies”
cards.description: Columbus landed in the Caribbean but thought he had reached the Indies near Asia.

cards.title: The Columbian Exchange
cards.description: A massive swap of plants, animals, people, and diseases flowed between the worlds.

cards.title: New Foods for the Old World
cards.description: The Americas gave the world potatoes, tomatoes, corn, and chocolate.

cards.title: New Animals for the Americas
cards.description: The Americas received horses, cattle, wheat, and honeybees from Europe.

cards.title: Disease Devastates Native Peoples
cards.description: Europeans unknowingly brought diseases that devastated Native populations.

cards.title: The Spanish Conquistadors
cards.description: Spanish explorers called conquistadors arrived seeking gold and riches.

cards.title: Ponce de León in Florida
cards.description: Juan Ponce de León explored Florida in 1513, searching for gold and youth.

cards.title: St. Augustine Founded
cards.description: Spain founded St. Augustine in Florida in 1565.

cards.title: America’s Oldest City
cards.description: St. Augustine is the oldest continuously inhabited European-founded city in the U.S.

cards.title: French Exploration of Canada
cards.description: French explorer Jacques Cartier explored the St. Lawrence River area.

cards.title: The French Fur Trade
cards.description: The French focused heavily on the highly lucrative fur trade.

cards.title: Henry Hudson Explores
cards.description: English explorer Henry Hudson explored the river and bay now named for him.

cards.title: England Wants Colonies
cards.description: England wanted colonies to match the growing wealth and power of Spain.

cards.title: The Roanoke Colony
cards.description: Sir Walter Raleigh sponsored England’s first attempt to colonize Roanoke Island.

cards.title: The Lost Colony
cards.description: The Roanoke colony completely vanished by 1590, leaving a lasting mystery.

cards.title: The “Croatoan” Clue
cards.description: The only clue left at Roanoke was the word “Croatoan” carved into a post.

cards.title: Jamestown Is Founded
cards.description: English settlers built Jamestown in Virginia — the first permanent English colony in America.

cards.title: The First Permanent English Colony
cards.description: Jamestown became the very first permanent English settlement in North America.

cards.title: The "Starving Time"
cards.description: The early Jamestown settlers suffered heavily from hunger, disease, and cold.

cards.title: Captain John Smith Takes Charge
cards.description: Captain John Smith took leadership of Jamestown to save it from collapse.

cards.title: "He Who Will Not Work…"
cards.description: Smith’s famous rule for the settlers was: "He who will not work shall not eat."

cards.title: Pocahontas
cards.description: Pocahontas was the daughter of Powhatan, a powerful local Native chief.

cards.title: A Fragile Peace
cards.description: Pocahontas helped keep peace between her tribe and the English settlers.

cards.title: Tobacco Saves Virginia
cards.description: Tobacco became Virginia’s cash crop, making the colony highly profitable.

cards.title: First Enslaved Africans
cards.description: In 1619, the first enslaved Africans were brought to Virginia.

cards.title: The House of Burgesses
cards.description: In 1619, the House of Burgesses met, starting representative government in America.

cards.title: The Pilgrims and the Mayflower
cards.description: The Pilgrims sailed to America in 1620 on a ship called the Mayflower.

cards.title: Who Were the Pilgrims?
cards.description: The Pilgrims were Separatists who wanted total freedom from the Church of England.

cards.title: The Mayflower Compact
cards.description: They signed the Mayflower Compact to create fair laws for their new colony.

cards.title: Landing at Plymouth
cards.description: The Pilgrims landed at Plymouth Rock in modern-day Massachusetts.

cards.title: Squanto Helps the Pilgrims
cards.description: Squanto, a Patuxet Native American, taught the Pilgrims how to plant corn using fish.

cards.title: The First Thanksgiving
cards.description: In autumn 1621, the Pilgrims and Wampanoag celebrated the first Thanksgiving.

cards.title: The Puritans Arrive
cards.description: The Puritans arrived in 1630, founding the Massachusetts Bay Colony.

cards.title: Why "Puritans"?
cards.description: The Puritans wanted to reform, or "purify," the Church of England.

cards.title: Boston, a Trading Hub
cards.description: Boston quickly grew into a major shipping and trading hub for New England.

cards.title: Three Regions of Colonies
cards.description: The British colonies were divided into three regions: New England, Middle, and Southern.

cards.title: The New England Colonies
cards.description: New England colonies included Massachusetts, Connecticut, Rhode Island, and New Hampshire.

cards.title: Rocky Soil, Long Winters
cards.description: New England had rocky soil, long winters, and plenty of thick forests.

cards.title: Fishing, Ships, and Trade
cards.description: The New England economy relied on shipbuilding, fishing, and ocean trade.

cards.title: Roger Williams & Rhode Island
cards.description: Roger Williams founded Rhode Island to offer true religious freedom.

cards.title: Anne Hutchinson
cards.description: Anne Hutchinson was banished from Massachusetts for preaching her own religious ideas.

cards.title: The Middle Colonies
cards.description: The Middle Colonies included New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, and Delaware.

cards.title: The "Breadbasket"
cards.description: The Middle Colonies were nicknamed the "Breadbasket" because they grew so much wheat.

cards.title: New Netherland (Dutch New York)
cards.description: New York was originally a Dutch colony called New Netherland.

cards.title: England Takes New York
cards.description: The English took over New Netherland in 1664 without firing a single shot.

cards.title: William Penn & Pennsylvania
cards.description: William Penn founded Pennsylvania as a safe refuge for Quakers.

cards.title: Philadelphia
cards.description: Philadelphia, Pennsylvania’s capital, means "The City of Brotherly Love."

cards.title: The Southern Colonies
cards.description: The Southern Colonies were Maryland, Virginia, the Carolinas, and Georgia.

cards.title: Plantations
cards.description: The Southern economy relied on large farms called plantations.

cards.title: Cash Crops
cards.description: Southern plantations grew cash crops like tobacco, rice, and indigo dye.

cards.title: Forced Labor
cards.description: Plantations depended heavily on the forced labor of enslaved people.

cards.title: Maryland, a Catholic Haven
cards.description: Maryland was founded by Lord Baltimore as a safe haven for Catholics.

cards.title: Georgia, a Fresh Start
cards.description: James Oglethorpe founded Georgia as a colony for debtors to start over.

cards.title: Georgia as a Buffer
cards.description: Georgia also served as a military buffer against Spanish-owned Florida.

cards.title: Benjamin Franklin, Inventor
cards.description: Benjamin Franklin was an inventor who created the lightning rod and bifocals.

cards.title: Poor Richard’s Almanack
cards.description: Franklin published Poor Richard’s Almanack, filled with wise, witty sayings.

cards.title: The Great Awakening
cards.description: The Great Awakening was a major religious revival movement in the 1730s and 1740s.

cards.title: Everyday Colonial Life
cards.description: Most colonists lived on small family farms and made their own clothes.

cards.title: Learning with Hornbooks
cards.description: Hornbooks — wooden paddles with lesson sheets — were used to teach reading.

cards.title: Colonial Children’s Games
cards.description: Colonial children played games like marbles, hopscotch, and rolling hoops.

cards.title: The French and Indian War
cards.description: The French and Indian War broke out between Britain and France in 1754.

cards.title: Fight for the Ohio Valley
cards.description: Both sides fought fiercely for control of the fertile Ohio River Valley.

cards.title: Native Nations Choose Sides
cards.description: Many Native American tribes allied with the French against the British.

cards.title: Young George Washington
cards.description: A young George Washington fought as a British military officer during this war.

cards.title: Britain Wins the War
cards.description: Great Britain won the French and Indian War in 1763.

cards.title: The Treaty of Paris (1763)
cards.description: The Treaty of Paris of 1763 officially ended the war.

cards.title: France Loses North America
cards.description: France lost almost all of its North American territory to Great Britain.

cards.title: A Mountain of Debt
cards.description: The war left Great Britain with a massive national debt.

cards.title: The Proclamation of 1763
cards.description: King George III issued the Proclamation of 1763 to stop westward settlement.

cards.title: Closing the Frontier
cards.description: The Proclamation forbade colonists from settling west of the Appalachian Mountains.

cards.title: Britain Decides to Tax
cards.description: Parliament decided to tax the colonists to pay off the massive war debt.

cards.title: The Sugar Act
cards.description: The Sugar Act of 1764 placed taxes on sugar and molasses imports.

cards.title: The Stamp Act
cards.description: The Stamp Act of 1765 taxed paper items like newspapers and playing cards.

cards.title: "No Taxation Without Representation"
cards.description: Colonists protested using the slogan: "No taxation without representation!"

cards.title: The Quartering Act
cards.description: The Quartering Act forced colonists to provide housing for British soldiers.

cards.title: The Sons of Liberty
cards.description: The Sons of Liberty formed as a secret group to protest British taxes.

cards.title: The Townshend Acts
cards.description: The Townshend Acts of 1767 taxed everyday imports like glass, lead, paint, and tea.

cards.title: Colonists Boycott British Goods
cards.description: Colonists boycotted British goods, refusing to buy them to show resistance.

cards.title: The Boston Massacre
cards.description: The Boston Massacre happened in 1770 when British soldiers fired into an angry crowd.

cards.title: Crispus Attucks
cards.description: Crispus Attucks, an African-Native American man, was the first killed at Boston.

cards.title: The Tax on Tea
cards.description: Parliament repealed most taxes but kept the tax on tea to prove its authority.

cards.title: The Boston Tea Party
cards.description: The Boston Tea Party took place on December 16, 1773.

cards.title: Disguised as Mohawks
cards.description: The Sons of Liberty disguised themselves as Mohawk Indians and boarded tea ships.

cards.title: 342 Chests of Tea
cards.description: They dumped 342 chests of British tea directly into Boston Harbor.

cards.title: The Coercive (Intolerable) Acts
cards.description: Britain passed the Coercive Acts, which colonists called the Intolerable Acts.

cards.title: Boston Harbor Closed
cards.description: The Intolerable Acts closed Boston Harbor and banned local town meetings.

cards.title: The First Continental Congress
cards.description: The First Continental Congress met in Philadelphia in 1774 to protest.

cards.title: The Minutemen
cards.description: Colonists formed volunteer citizen militias known proudly as Minutemen.

cards.title: Ready in a Minute
cards.description: Minutemen earned their name because they could be ready to fight in a minute.

cards.title: Paul Revere’s Midnight Ride
cards.description: Paul Revere made his famous midnight ride to warn that British troops were coming.

cards.title: The Revolutionary War Begins
cards.description: The Revolutionary War began on April 19, 1775, in Massachusetts.

cards.title: Lexington and Concord
cards.description: The battles of Lexington and Concord marked the start of the war.

cards.title: "The Shot Heard ’Round the World"
cards.description: The opening shot at Lexington is called "the shot heard ’round the world."

cards.title: The Second Continental Congress
cards.description: The Second Continental Congress created the official Continental Army.

cards.title: Washington Takes Command
cards.description: George Washington was chosen as the Commander-in-Chief of the army.

cards.title: The Battle of Bunker Hill
cards.description: The Battle of Bunker Hill showed the British that Americans would fight hard.

cards.title: Thomas Paine’s "Common Sense"
cards.description: Thomas Paine wrote a pamphlet called Common Sense urging independence.

cards.title: Jefferson Writes the Draft
cards.description: Thomas Jefferson wrote the primary draft of the Declaration of Independence.

cards.title: "Life, Liberty, and Happiness"
cards.description: The Declaration says all people have rights to "Life, Liberty and the pursuit of Happiness."

cards.title: The Declaration of Independence
cards.description: The Continental Congress officially adopted the Declaration on July 4, 1776.

cards.title: Independence Day
cards.description: July 4 is celebrated every year as America’s Independence Day.

cards.title: Patriots
cards.description: People who supported independence were called Patriots or Whigs.

cards.title: Loyalists
cards.description: People who wanted to stay loyal to the King were called Loyalists or Tories.

cards.title: Crossing the Delaware
cards.description: On Christmas night 1776, Washington crossed the icy Delaware River.

cards.title: Victory at Trenton
cards.description: Washington led a surprise attack on Hessian forces in Trenton, New Jersey.

cards.title: The Turning Point
cards.description: Saratoga: The American victory at the Battle of Saratoga was the major turning point.

cards.title: France Joins the Fight
cards.description: Saratoga convinced France to sign an alliance and help the American cause.

cards.title: Winter at Valley Forge
cards.description: The Continental Army spent a brutal, freezing winter at Valley Forge.

cards.title: Baron von Steuben
cards.description: Baron von Steuben trained the soldiers at Valley Forge into a professional army.

cards.title: The Marquis de Lafayette
cards.description: Marquis de Lafayette was a young French noble who volunteered to help Washington.

cards.title: John Paul Jones
cards.description: John Paul Jones was a naval hero who declared, "I have not yet begun to fight!"

cards.title: Benedict Arnold’s Betrayal
cards.description: Benedict Arnold was an American general who infamously switched sides to the British.

cards.title: General Cornwallis
cards.description: General Cornwallis led the British army in the Southern colonies.

cards.title: The Battle of Yorktown
cards.description: The final major battle of the war was the Battle of Yorktown in 1781.

cards.title: Cornwallis Surrenders
cards.description: Surrounded by French ships and American troops, Cornwallis surrendered at Yorktown.

cards.title: The Treaty of Paris (1783)
cards.description: The Treaty of Paris of 1783 officially recognized American independence.

cards.title: The Articles of Confederation
cards.description: The Articles of Confederation served as the first, very weak U.S. government.

cards.title: A Government Too Weak
cards.description: Under the Articles, the federal government could not collect taxes or print money.

cards.title: Shays’ Rebellion
cards.description: Shays’ Rebellion in 1786 showed that the weak government could not maintain order.

cards.title: The Constitutional Convention
cards.description: Constitutional Convention delegates met in Philadelphia in 1787 to fix the government.

cards.title: A Brand-New Constitution
cards.description: Instead of fixing the Articles, they wrote an entirely new U.S. Constitution.

cards.title: "Father of the Constitution"
cards.description: James Madison is called the "Father of the Constitution" for his major role.

cards.title: Three Branches
cards.description: The Constitution divided the government into three separate branches.

cards.title: The Legislative Branch
cards.description: The Legislative Branch (Congress) makes the nation’s laws.

cards.title: The Executive Branch
cards.description: The Executive Branch (the President) enforces the nation’s laws.

cards.title: The Judicial Branch
cards.description: The Judicial Branch (the Supreme Court) interprets the nation’s laws.

cards.title: Checks and Balances
cards.description: A system of checks and balances prevents any single branch from becoming too powerful.

cards.title: The Great Compromise
cards.description: The Great Compromise created a two-house Congress: the Senate and House of Representatives.

cards.title: Federalists vs. Anti-Federalists
cards.description: Federalists supported the Constitution; Anti-Federalists worried it gave government too much power.

cards.title: The Bill of Rights
cards.description: To protect citizen rights, the Bill of Rights was added to the Constitution.

cards.title: The First Ten Amendments
cards.description: The Bill of Rights consists of the first ten amendments to the Constitution.

cards.title: The First Amendment
cards.description: The First Amendment protects freedom of speech, religion, press, and assembly.

cards.title: Washington, First President
cards.description: George Washington was unanimously elected as the first President of the United States.

cards.title: The First Inauguration
cards.description: Washington took the oath of office in New York City, the temporary capital.

cards.title: Stepping Down After Two Terms
cards.description: Washington chose to step down after two terms, setting an important future precedent.

cards.title: John Adams, Second President
cards.description: John Adams was elected as the second President of the United States.

cards.title: The First White House Resident
cards.description: Adams was the very first president to live in the newly built White House.

cards.title: Thomas Jefferson, Third President
cards.description: Thomas Jefferson was elected as the third President of the United States.

cards.title: The Louisiana Purchase
cards.description: In 1803, Jefferson purchased the Louisiana Territory from France for $15 million.

cards.title: Doubling the Nation
cards.description: The Louisiana Purchase instantly doubled the geographic size of the nation.

cards.title: Lewis and Clark
cards.description: Meriwether Lewis and William Clark were hired to explore the new western land.

cards.title: The Corps of Discovery
cards.description: Their expedition team was officially called the Corps of Discovery.

cards.title: Sacagawea
cards.description: A Shoshone woman named Sacagawea served as their vital guide and translator.

cards.title: Reaching the Pacific
cards.description: The expedition reached the Pacific Ocean in 1805 and mapped the wilderness.

cards.title: The War of 1812
cards.description: The War of 1812 broke out between the United States and Great Britain.

cards.title: Impressment at Sea
cards.description: A major cause of the war was the British impressment (kidnapping) of American sailors.

cards.title: Washington Burns
cards.description: During the war, British troops marched into Washington, D.C., and burned the White House.

cards.title: Dolley Madison’s Rescue
cards.description: First Lady Dolley Madison saved a famous portrait of George Washington from the fire.

cards.title: Francis Scott Key’s Poem
cards.description: Francis Scott Key wrote a poem during the bombardment of Fort McHenry.

cards.title: "The Star-Spangled Banner"
cards.description: This famous poem later became "The Star-Spangled Banner," America’s national anthem.

cards.title: The Battle of New Orleans
cards.description: General Andrew Jackson became a national hero at the Battle of New Orleans.

cards.title: The Treaty of Ghent
cards.description: The Treaty of Ghent ended the War of 1812, restoring peace.

cards.title: The Industrial Revolution
cards.description: The Industrial Revolution began changing how goods were made, from hand tools to machines.

cards.title: Eli Whitney’s Cotton Gin
cards.description: Eli Whitney invented the cotton gin in 1793, speeding up cotton seed removal.

cards.title: A Tragic Side Effect
cards.description: The cotton gin unintentionally caused a massive increase in the demand for enslaved labor.

cards.title: The Erie Canal
cards.description: The Erie Canal opened in 1825, connecting the Hudson River to the Great Lakes.

cards.title: New York Rises
cards.description: The canal made New York City the nation’s premier center of commerce.

cards.title: The Monroe Doctrine
cards.description: The Monroe Doctrine of 1823 warned European nations to stay out of the Americas.

cards.title: Andrew Jackson Elected
cards.description: Andrew Jackson was elected as the seventh U.S. President in 1828.

cards.title: The Indian Removal Act
cards.description: Jackson signed the devastating Indian Removal Act into law in 1830.

cards.title: Forced From Their Lands
cards.description: Native American tribes were forced to leave their ancestral lands in the Southeast.

cards.title: The Long March West
cards.description: They were forced to march hundreds of miles to Indian Territory in modern Oklahoma.

cards.title: The Trail of Tears
cards.description: This forced march is known as the Trail of Tears because thousands died.

cards.title: Manifest Destiny
cards.description: "Manifest Destiny" was the widespread belief that America should expand coast to coast.

cards.title: Texas Fights for Independence
cards.description: Texas fought for its independence from Mexico in the year 1836.

cards.title: The Battle of the Alamo
cards.description: The Battle of the Alamo was a famous siege where Texan defenders were defeated.

cards.title: "Remember the Alamo!"
cards.description: "Remember the Alamo!" became the rallying cry for Texan independence.

cards.title: The Republic of Texas
cards.description: Texas existed as an independent republic before joining the United States in 1845.

cards.title: The Mexican-American War
cards.description: The Mexican-American War began in 1846 over a border dispute in Texas.

cards.title: A Vast New Territory
cards.description: The U.S. won the war, gaining land that became California, Utah, Nevada, and Arizona.

cards.title: The Oregon Trail
cards.description: The Oregon Trail was a 2,000-mile route used by thousands of pioneers moving west.

cards.title: Wagon Trains
cards.description: Pioneers traveled the long trails together in large groups called wagon trains.

cards.title: Gold at Sutter’s Mill
cards.description: Gold was discovered at Sutter’s Mill in California in 1848.

cards.title: The Forty-Niners
cards.description: In 1849, over 80,000 gold-seekers rushed to California; they were called "49ers."

cards.title: California Becomes a State
cards.description: The California Gold Rush led to rapid population growth and statehood by 1850.

cards.title: The Steam Locomotive
cards.description: Steam locomotives began replacing horses, revolutionizing long-distance travel.

cards.title: Morse and the Telegraph
cards.description: Samuel Morse invented the telegraph and Morse code, making instant communication possible.

cards.title: The Abolitionist Movement
cards.description: The abolitionist movement grew quickly, dedicated to ending slavery in America.

cards.title: The Underground Railroad
cards.description: The Underground Railroad was a secret network helping enslaved people escape north.

cards.title: Harriet Tubman
cards.description: Harriet Tubman escaped slavery in 1849 and risked her life to guide others to freedom.

cards.title: "Moses" of Her People
cards.description: Tubman was proudly nicknamed "Moses" for leading her people to freedom.

cards.title: Frederick Douglass
cards.description: Frederick Douglass escaped slavery and became a powerful writer, orator, and activist.

cards.title: Uncle Tom’s Cabin
cards.description: Harriet Beecher Stowe wrote Uncle Tom’s Cabin, a book that exposed the horrors of slavery.

cards.title: The Seneca Falls Convention
cards.description: The Seneca Falls Convention of 1848 was the first women’s rights convention in America.

cards.title: The Declaration of Sentiments
cards.description: Elizabeth Cady Stanton wrote the Declaration of Sentiments demanding women’s right to vote.

cards.title: The Missouri Compromise
cards.description: The Missouri Compromise of 1820 tried to balance free and slave states.

cards.title: The Compromise of 1850
cards.description: The Compromise of 1850 included the strict Fugitive Slave Act.

cards.title: The Fugitive Slave Act
cards.description: The Fugitive Slave Act required citizens to help capture escaped enslaved people.

cards.title: "Bleeding Kansas"
cards.description: "Bleeding Kansas" was a period of violent conflict over whether Kansas would allow slavery.

cards.title: The Dred Scott Decision
cards.description: The Supreme Court’s Dred Scott decision ruled that enslaved people were not citizens.

cards.title: Lincoln Is Elected
cards.description: Abraham Lincoln was elected as the 16th President of the United States in 1860.

cards.title: South Carolina Secedes
cards.description: South Carolina became the very first state to secede (leave) from the Union.

cards.title: The Confederacy Forms
cards.description: Eleven Southern states seceded to form the Confederate States of America.

cards.title: Jefferson Davis
cards.description: Jefferson Davis was chosen as the President of the Confederacy.

cards.title: The Civil War Begins
cards.description: The Civil War began on April 12, 1861, at Fort Sumter, South Carolina.

cards.title: Fort Sumter Falls
cards.description: Confederate forces fired on the federal fort, forcing its surrender.

cards.title: The Union (the North)
cards.description: The North was called the Union, and their soldiers wore blue uniforms.

cards.title: The Confederacy (the South)
cards.description: The South was called the Confederacy, and their soldiers wore gray uniforms.

cards.title: The Union’s Strengths
cards.description: The Union had more factories, railroads, and a much larger population.

cards.title: The Confederacy’s Strengths
cards.description: The Confederacy had excellent military generals and fought on familiar home territory.

cards.title: The First Battle of Bull Run
cards.description: The First Battle of Bull Run was the first major land battle of the war.

cards.title: "Stonewall" Jackson
cards.description: Confederate General Thomas Jackson earned his famous nickname "Stonewall" at Bull Run.

cards.title: General Robert E. Lee
cards.description: General Robert E. Lee was chosen to command the Confederate Army of Northern Virginia.

cards.title: The Battle of Antietam
cards.description: The Battle of Antietam in 1862 was the single bloodiest day in American military history.

cards.title: The Emancipation Proclamation
cards.description: President Lincoln issued the historic Emancipation Proclamation on January 1, 1863.

cards.title: Declaring Freedom
cards.description: The Proclamation declared that all enslaved people in Confederate-held lands were free.

cards.title: Black Soldiers Join the Fight
cards.description: It also allowed African American men to officially enlist in the Union Army.

cards.title: The 54th Massachusetts
cards.description: The 54th Massachusetts Infantry was one of the most famous all-Black Union regiments.

cards.title: Clara Barton
cards.description: Clara Barton worked as a frontline nurse and later founded the American Red Cross.

cards.title: The Battle of Gettysburg
cards.description: The Battle of Gettysburg in July 1863 was the ultimate turning point of the war.

cards.title: Lee’s Invasion Ends
cards.description: The Union victory at Gettysburg ended General Robert E. Lee’s invasion of the North.

cards.title: The Fall of Vicksburg
cards.description: General Ulysses S. Grant captured Vicksburg, giving the Union control of the Mississippi River.

cards.title: The Gettysburg Address
cards.description: Lincoln delivered the timeless Gettysburg Address to dedicate a national cemetery.

cards.title: "Four Score and Seven…"
cards.description: The short speech begins with the famous words: "Four score and seven years ago..."

cards.title: Sherman’s March to the Sea
cards.description: Union General William T. Sherman led a destructive "March to the Sea" through Georgia.

cards.title: Lee Surrenders
cards.description: General Robert E. Lee surrendered to General Ulysses S. Grant on April 9, 1865.

cards.title: Appomattox Court House
cards.description: The surrender took place at Appomattox Court House in Virginia, ending the war.

cards.title: Lincoln Is Assassinated
cards.description: On April 14, 1865, President Lincoln was assassinated by John Wilkes Booth.

cards.title: Ford’s Theatre
cards.description: Lincoln was shot while watching a play at Ford’s Theatre in Washington, D.C.

cards.title: Reconstruction
cards.description: Reconstruction was the era dedicated to rebuilding the South and reuniting the country.

cards.title: The 13th Amendment
cards.description: The 13th Amendment was ratified, completely abolishing slavery in the United States.

cards.title: The 14th Amendment
cards.description: The 14th Amendment granted full citizenship to all people born in the United States.

cards.title: The 15th Amendment
cards.description: The 15th Amendment protected the right to vote regardless of race or color.

cards.title: The Freedmen’s Bureau
cards.description: The Freedmen’s Bureau was established to help former slaves find jobs and get an education.

cards.title: President Andrew Johnson
cards.description: Andrew Johnson became president after Lincoln’s death and faced impeachment by Congress.

cards.title: Sharecropping
cards.description: Sharecropping became common in the South, keeping many freed people trapped in deep debt.

cards.title: Jim Crow Laws
cards.description: "Jim Crow" laws were passed across the South to enforce racial segregation.

cards.title: Segregation
cards.description: Segregation meant separating Black and white Americans in public spaces.

cards.title: The Transcontinental Railroad
cards.description: The Transcontinental Railroad was completed in 1869 at Promontory Summit, Utah.

cards.title: The Golden Spike
cards.description: A golden spike was driven into the ground to connect the Atlantic and Pacific rails.

cards.title: The Railroad Workers
cards.description: Thousands of Chinese and Irish immigrants built the dangerous Transcontinental Railroad.

cards.title: The Homestead Act
cards.description: The Homestead Act of 1862 offered 160 acres of free western land to settlers.

cards.title: Earning the Land
cards.description: Settlers had to live on the land and farm it for five years to own it.

cards.title: The Buffalo Soldiers
cards.description: Buffalo Soldiers were elite regiments of African American cavalrymen serving out west.

cards.title: Reconstruction Ends
cards.description: Reconstruction officially ended in 1877 when federal troops left the South.

cards.era: The Industrial Era & World War I
cards.title: The Gilded Age
cards.description: The Gilded Age was a time of massive economic growth but severe hidden poverty.

cards.era: The Industrial Era & World War I
cards.title: The Telephone
cards.description: Alexander Graham Bell invented the telephone in 1876, changing communication forever.

cards.era: The Industrial Era & World War I
cards.title: Edison’s Lightbulb
cards.description: Thomas Edison perfected the incandescent electric lightbulb at his Menlo Park lab.

cards.era: The Industrial Era & World War I
cards.title: The Wizard of Menlo Park
cards.description: Edison held over 1,000 patents, earning him the nickname "The Wizard of Menlo Park."

cards.era: The Industrial Era & World War I
cards.title: Captains of Industry
cards.description: Corporations grew rapidly, led by incredibly wealthy "captains of industry."

cards.era: The Industrial Era & World War I
cards.title: Andrew Carnegie
cards.description: Andrew Carnegie dominated the steel industry and later gave away his fortune to libraries.

cards.era: The Industrial Era & World War I
cards.title: John D. Rockefeller
cards.description: John D. Rockefeller founded Standard Oil, becoming America’s very first billionaire.

cards.era: The Industrial Era & World War I
cards.title: Ellis Island Opens
cards.description: Ellis Island opened in New York Harbor in 1892 as an immigration processing station.

cards.era: The Industrial Era & World War I
cards.title: A Nation of Immigrants
cards.description: More than 12 million immigrants entered the United States through Ellis Island.

cards.era: The Industrial Era & World War I
cards.title: Angel Island
cards.description: Angel Island opened in San Francisco in 1910, processing mostly Asian immigrants.

cards.era: The Industrial Era & World War I
cards.title: Urbanization
cards.description: Cities grew rapidly, a trend known as urbanization.

cards.era: The Industrial Era & World War I
cards.title: Tenement Life
cards.description: Many poor immigrant families lived in crowded, unsafe apartment buildings called tenements.

cards.era: The Industrial Era & World War I
cards.title: Labor Unions
cards.description: Labor unions formed to fight for better pay, shorter hours, and safer working conditions.

cards.era: The Industrial Era & World War I
cards.title: Jane Addams and Hull House
cards.description: Jane Addams founded Hull House in Chicago to help poor immigrants adjust to city life.

cards.era: The Industrial Era & World War I
cards.title: The Spanish-American War
cards.description: The Spanish-American War broke out in 1898 after the USS Maine exploded in Cuba.

cards.era: The Industrial Era & World War I
cards.title: The Rough Riders
cards.description: Theodore Roosevelt led a famous volunteer cavalry unit called the "Rough Riders."

cards.era: The Industrial Era & World War I
cards.title: America Gains Territory
cards.description: The U.S. won the war, gaining control of Puerto Rico, Guam, and the Philippines.

cards.era: The Industrial Era & World War I
cards.title: The Progressive Era
cards.description: The Progressive Era was a period focused on fixing social and political problems.

cards.era: The Industrial Era & World War I
cards.title: The Muckrakers
cards.description: "Muckrakers" were journalists who exposed corruption and bad conditions in society.

cards.era: The Industrial Era & World War I
cards.title: The Jungle
cards.description: Upton Sinclair wrote The Jungle, exposing unsanitary conditions in the meatpacking industry.

cards.era: The Industrial Era & World War I
cards.title: The Pure Food and Drug Act
cards.description: Sinclair’s book led directly to the passage of the Pure Food and Drug Act.

cards.era: The Industrial Era & World War I
cards.title: President Theodore Roosevelt
cards.description: Theodore Roosevelt became president in 1901 after William McKinley’s assassination.

cards.era: The Industrial Era & World War I
cards.title: Roosevelt the Conservationist
cards.description: Roosevelt was a passionate conservationist who created the U.S. Forest Service.

cards.era: The Industrial Era & World War I
cards.title: Protecting the Land
cards.description: Roosevelt established 5 national parks and protected 150 national forests.

cards.era: The Industrial Era & World War I
cards.title: The Wright Brothers
cards.description: Orville and Wilbur Wright made the first successful controlled airplane flight in 1903.

cards.era: The Industrial Era & World War I
cards.title: Kitty Hawk
cards.description: The historic Wright brothers’ flight took place at Kitty Hawk, North Carolina.

cards.era: The Industrial Era & World War I
cards.title: The Model T
cards.description: Henry Ford introduced the Model T automobile in 1908, making cars affordable.

cards.era: The Industrial Era & World War I
cards.title: The Assembly Line
cards.description: Ford revolutionized manufacturing by using the moving assembly line.

cards.era: The Industrial Era & World War I
cards.title: The Panama Canal
cards.description: The United States built the Panama Canal, opening a vital shipping shortcut in 1914.

cards.era: The Industrial Era & World War I
cards.title: World War I Begins
cards.description: World War I began in Europe in 1914 between the Allied and Central Powers.

cards.era: The Industrial Era & World War I
cards.title: Trying to Stay Out
cards.description: President Woodrow Wilson tried hard to keep the United States out of the conflict.

cards.era: The Industrial Era & World War I
cards.title: German U-Boats
cards.description: Germany used submarines called U-boats to sink American merchant ships.

cards.era: The Industrial Era & World War I
cards.title: The Lusitania
cards.description: The sinking of the British passenger liner Lusitania in 1915 killed 128 Americans.

cards.era: The Industrial Era & World War I
cards.title: The Zimmerman Telegram
cards.description: The Zimmerman Telegram revealed Germany’s secret plan to get Mexico to attack the U.S.

cards.era: The Industrial Era & World War I
cards.title: America Enters the War
cards.description: The United States officially entered World War I on the Allied side in 1917.

cards.era: The Industrial Era & World War I
cards.title: The Doughboys
cards.description: American soldiers in World War I were affectionately nicknamed "Doughboys."

cards.era: The Industrial Era & World War I
cards.title: General Pershing
cards.description: General John J. Pershing led the American Expeditionary Forces in Europe.

cards.era: The Industrial Era & World War I
cards.title: The War Ends
cards.description: World War I officially ended on November 11, 1918, with an Allied victory.

cards.era: The Industrial Era & World War I
cards.title: Veterans Day
cards.description: November 11 is now celebrated every year in America as Veterans Day.

cards.era: The Industrial Era & World War I
cards.title: The League of Nations
cards.description: President Wilson proposed the League of Nations to help prevent future world wars.

cards.era: The Industrial Era & World War I
cards.title: The 18th Amendment
cards.description: The 18th Amendment was ratified, banning the sale and manufacturing of alcohol.

cards.era: The Industrial Era & World War I
cards.title: Prohibition
cards.description: This era of alcohol ban became known historically as Prohibition.

cards.era: The Industrial Era & World War I
cards.title: The 19th Amendment
cards.description: The 19th Amendment was proudly ratified in 1920, granting women the right to vote.

cards.era: The Industrial Era & World War I
cards.title: Susan B. Anthony
cards.description: Susan B. Anthony spent her life fighting for women’s suffrage but died before it passed.

cards.era: The Industrial Era & World War I
cards.title: The Roaring Twenties
cards.description: The 1920s were called the "Roaring Twenties" because the economy was booming.

cards.era: The Industrial Era & World War I
cards.title: The Jazz Age
cards.description: Jazz music became incredibly popular, making the 1920s the "Jazz Age."

cards.era: The Industrial Era & World War I
cards.title: The Harlem Renaissance
cards.description: The Harlem Renaissance was a massive explosion of African American art, literature, and music.

cards.era: The Industrial Era & World War I
cards.title: Langston Hughes
cards.description: Langston Hughes became a famous poet during the Harlem Renaissance.

cards.era: The Industrial Era & World War I
cards.title: The Age of Radio
cards.description: Commercial radio stations began broadcasting, bringing news and music into living rooms.

cards.era: The Industrial Era & World War I
cards.title: Lindbergh Crosses the Atlantic
cards.description: Charles Lindbergh made the first solo nonstop flight across the Atlantic Ocean in 1927.

cards.era: The Great Depression & World War II
cards.title: Black Tuesday
cards.description: The U.S. stock market crashed on "Black Tuesday," October 29, 1929.

cards.era: The Great Depression & World War II
cards.title: The Great Depression
cards.description: The crash marked the start of the Great Depression, the worst economic downturn in history.

cards.era: The Great Depression & World War II
cards.title: One in Four Out of Work
cards.description: By 1933, one out of every four American workers had lost their job.

cards.era: The Great Depression & World War II
cards.title: The Dust Bowl
cards.description: Massive droughts turned the Great Plains into what was called the "Dust Bowl."

cards.era: The Great Depression & World War II
cards.title: The Dust Storms
cards.description: Giant, blinding dust storms destroyed farms, forcing families to move west.

cards.era: The Great Depression & World War II
cards.title: Hoovervilles
cards.description: Shantytowns built by homeless people were nicknamed "Hoovervilles" after President Hoover.

cards.era: The Great Depression & World War II
cards.title: FDR Is Elected
cards.description: Franklin D. Roosevelt (FDR) was elected president in 1932, promising hope.

cards.era: The Great Depression & World War II
cards.title: The Fireside Chats
cards.description: Roosevelt gave weekly radio speeches called "fireside chats" to reassure the public.

cards.era: The Great Depression & World War II
cards.title: The New Deal
cards.description: FDR launched the "New Deal," a massive collection of government recovery programs.

cards.era: The Great Depression & World War II
cards.title: The Civilian Conservation Corps
cards.description: The Civilian Conservation Corps (CCC) hired young men to plant trees and build parks.

cards.era: The Great Depression & World War II
cards.title: The Social Security Act
cards.description: The Social Security Act was passed to provide retirement pensions for older Americans.

cards.era: The Great Depression & World War II
cards.title: World War II Begins
cards.description: World War II began in Europe in 1939 when Germany invaded Poland.

cards.era: The Great Depression & World War II
cards.title: Axis vs. Allies
cards.description: The war was fought between the Axis Powers and the Allied Powers.

cards.era: The Great Depression & World War II
cards.title: America Stays Neutral
cards.description: The United States stayed neutral at first, but provided supplies to Great Britain.

cards.era: The Great Depression & World War II
cards.title: The Attack on Pearl Harbor
cards.description: Japan launched a surprise air attack on the U.S. naval base at Pearl Harbor, Hawaii.

cards.era: The Great Depression & World War II
cards.title: December 7, 1941
cards.description: The attack on Pearl Harbor occurred on the morning of December 7, 1941.

cards.era: The Great Depression & World War II
cards.title: "A Date Which Will Live in Infamy"
cards.description: FDR famously called December 7 "a date which will live in infamy."

cards.era: The Great Depression & World War II
cards.title: America Enters the War
cards.description: The United States officially entered World War II the very next day.

cards.era: The Great Depression & World War II
cards.title: Women on the Home Front
cards.description: Millions of American women took over factory jobs to build war planes and tanks.

cards.era: The Great Depression & World War II
cards.title: Rosie the Riveter
cards.description: "Rosie the Riveter" became a famous symbol of women working in wartime factories.

cards.era: The Great Depression & World War II
cards.title: The Tuskegee Airmen
cards.description: The Tuskegee Airmen were America’s first elite African American military pilots.

cards.era: The Great Depression & World War II
cards.title: The Navajo Code Talkers
cards.description: Navajo Code Talkers used their native language to send unbreakable secret codes.

cards.era: The Great Depression & World War II
cards.title: Japanese American Internment
cards.description: Over 110,000 Japanese Americans were unjustly forced into internment camps.

cards.era: The Great Depression & World War II
cards.title: General Eisenhower
cards.description: General Dwight D. Eisenhower served as the Supreme Allied Commander in Europe.

cards.era: The Great Depression & World War II
cards.title: D-Day
cards.description: D-Day took place on June 6, 1944, with a massive Allied invasion of Normandy, France.

cards.era: The Great Depression & World War II
cards.title: The Battle of the Bulge
cards.description: The Battle of the Bulge was Germany’s final major counterattack against Allied forces.

cards.era: The Great Depression & World War II
cards.title: FDR Dies; Truman Takes Over
cards.description: President Franklin D. Roosevelt died in April 1945, and Harry S. Truman became president.

cards.era: The Great Depression & World War II
cards.title: V-E Day
cards.description: Germany surrendered in May 1945, a day celebrated as V-E Day (Victory in Europe).

cards.era: The Great Depression & World War II
cards.title: The Holocaust
cards.description: The Holocaust was the horrific murder of six million Jews by the Nazi regime.

cards.era: The Great Depression & World War II
cards.title: The Atomic Bomb
cards.description: Truman authorized using the newly invented atomic bomb to bring a swift end to the war.

cards.era: The Great Depression & World War II
cards.title: Hiroshima and Nagasaki
cards.description: The U.S. dropped atomic bombs on the Japanese cities of Hiroshima and Nagasaki.

cards.era: The Great Depression & World War II
cards.title: Japan Surrenders
cards.description: Japan surrendered in August 1945, officially ending World War II.

cards.era: The Great Depression & World War II
cards.title: The United Nations
cards.description: The United Nations was formed in 1945 to maintain future international peace.

cards.title: Jackie Robinson
cards.description: Jackie Robinson shattered the color barrier in Major League Baseball in 1947.

cards.title: Number 42
cards.description: Robinson played for the Brooklyn Dodgers, wearing the famous number 42.

cards.title: The Cold War
cards.description: The Cold War was a decades-long rivalry between the U.S. and the Soviet Union.

cards.title: Superpowers
cards.description: The U.S. and the Soviet Union were called superpowers for their massive military and economic might.

cards.title: The Iron Curtain
cards.description: The "Iron Curtain" described the divide between democratic Western and communist Eastern Europe.

cards.title: Containment
cards.description: Containment was the U.S. strategy to stop the spread of communism around the world.

cards.title: The Marshall Plan
cards.description: The Marshall Plan gave billions of dollars to help rebuild Western Europe after WWII.

cards.title: NATO
cards.description: NATO was formed in 1949 as a military alliance to protect Western nations.

cards.title: The Berlin Airlift
cards.description: U.S. and British planes flew food and supplies into West Berlin after the Soviets blocked the roads.

cards.title: The Red Scare
cards.description: The Red Scare was a period of intense fear that communist spies were inside the U.S.

cards.title: Joseph McCarthy
cards.description: Senator Joseph McCarthy accused many innocent citizens of being secret communists.

cards.title: The Korean War
cards.description: The Korean War was fought to stop communist North Korea from taking over South Korea.

cards.title: The 38th Parallel
cards.description: The 38th Parallel is the line that divided North and South Korea.

cards.title: General MacArthur
cards.description: General Douglas MacArthur led United Nations forces during the Korean War.

cards.title: The Baby Boom
cards.description: The Baby Boom was a huge spike in births in the U.S. between 1946 and 1964.

cards.title: The Suburbs
cards.description: Suburbs were residential areas outside cities that grew rapidly in the 1950s.

cards.title: Levittown
cards.description: Levittown was the first mass-produced suburban housing development, built in New York.

cards.title: The Interstate Highways
cards.description: A massive network of highways was built across America, started by President Eisenhower.

cards.title: President Eisenhower
cards.description: Dwight D. Eisenhower, a famous WWII general, became the 34th President in 1953.

cards.title: The Television Takeover
cards.description: By the 1950s, television became the most popular form of entertainment in American homes.

cards.title: Rock and Roll
cards.description: Rock and roll, a new genre blending blues, country, and gospel, became a hit with 1950s teenagers.

cards.title: Elvis Presley
cards.description: Known as the "King of Rock and Roll," Elvis became a massive cultural icon in the 1950s.

cards.title: The Polio Vaccine
cards.description: Dr. Jonas Salk invented the polio vaccine in 1953, saving millions of children from paralysis.

cards.title: Sputnik
cards.description: Sputnik, the first artificial satellite, was launched by the Soviet Union, shocking Americans.

cards.title: The Space Race
cards.description: The Space Race was the intense competition between the U.S. and the Soviets to lead in spaceflight.

cards.title: NASA
cards.description: NASA was created by Congress in 1958 to lead America’s space efforts.

cards.title: Explorer 1
cards.description: Explorer 1 was the first successful satellite launched into space by the United States in 1958.

cards.title: Alaska Becomes a State
cards.description: Alaska was admitted to the Union as the 49th state of America in 1959.

cards.title: Hawaii Becomes a State
cards.description: Hawaii was admitted as the 50th and final state of America in 1959.

cards.title: The Berlin Wall
cards.description: The Berlin Wall was built in 1961 by East Germany to stop citizens escaping to West Berlin.

cards.title: The U-2 Incident
cards.description: The U-2 Incident was a crisis after a U.S. spy plane was shot down over the Soviet Union.

cards.title: Duck and Cover
cards.description: "Duck and Cover" was a safety drill taught to schoolchildren in case of a nuclear attack.

cards.title: The Peace Corps
cards.description: The Peace Corps was created by President Kennedy to send American volunteers to help developing nations.

cards.title: The Bay of Pigs
cards.description: The Bay of Pigs was a failed U.S.-backed invasion of Cuba aimed at overthrowing Fidel Castro.

cards.title: The Cuban Missile Crisis
cards.description: The Cuban Missile Crisis was a 13-day standoff over Soviet nuclear missiles in Cuba.

cards.title: President John F. Kennedy
cards.description: John F. Kennedy was the 35th President, known for his youthful energy and inspiring speeches.

cards.title: The JFK Assassination
cards.description: President Kennedy was shot and killed in Dallas, Texas, on November 22, 1963.

cards.title: Lyndon B. Johnson
cards.description: Vice President Lyndon B. Johnson was sworn in as the 36th President right after JFK’s death.

cards.title: The Great Society
cards.description: The Great Society was Johnson’s set of programs aimed at ending poverty and racial injustice.

cards.title: Medicare and Medicaid
cards.description: Medicare and Medicaid were health insurance programs created to help the elderly and the poor.

cards.title: Project Mercury
cards.description: Project Mercury was America’s first human spaceflight program, designed to put a person into orbit.

cards.title: John Glenn
cards.description: John Glenn became the first American astronaut to orbit the Earth in 1962.

cards.title: The Civil Rights Movement
cards.description: Across the 1950s and 60s, Americans fought peacefully to end unfair laws and win equal rights.

cards.title: Segregation
cards.description: Segregation was the legal separation of people by race, common in the South for decades.

cards.title: Jim Crow Laws
cards.description: Jim Crow laws enforced racial segregation in public places like schools and restaurants.

cards.title: Brown v. Board of Education
cards.description: This 1954 Supreme Court ruling declared segregated public schools unconstitutional.

cards.title: Thurgood Marshall
cards.description: Thurgood Marshall argued the Brown case and later became the first Black Supreme Court Justice.

cards.title: Rosa Parks
cards.description: Rosa Parks refused to give up her bus seat to a white man, sparking a massive protest.

cards.title: The Montgomery Bus Boycott
cards.description: For over a year, African Americans refused to ride city buses, forcing them to desegregate.

cards.title: Dr. Martin Luther King Jr.
cards.description: Dr. King, a Baptist minister, became the most famous leader of the nonviolent movement.

cards.title: Nonviolent Protest
cards.description: Nonviolent protest was a peaceful way of fighting injustice without using violence.

cards.title: The Little Rock Nine
cards.description: Nine Black students integrated an all-white high school under federal troop protection.

cards.title: The Sit-ins
cards.description: Activists sat at segregated lunch counters and refused to leave until they were served.

cards.title: The Freedom Riders
cards.description: Activists rode buses into the segregated South to protest illegal terminal segregation.

cards.title: The March on Washington
cards.description: Over 250,000 people rallied in 1963 demanding civil and economic rights for African Americans.

cards.title: "I Have a Dream"
cards.description: Dr. King’s legendary speech at the March on Washington called for equality and unity.

cards.title: The Civil Rights Act of 1964
cards.description: This landmark law banned discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, or origin.

cards.title: The Voting Rights Act of 1965
cards.description: This law outlawed unfair tricks used to stop African Americans from voting.

cards.title: The Selma Marches
cards.description: Three protest marches from Selma to Montgomery led directly to the Voting Rights Act.

cards.title: Malcolm X
cards.description: Malcolm X urged Black people to defend themselves and take pride in their heritage.

cards.title: The Chicano Movement
cards.description: The Chicano Movement was a civil rights movement led by Mexican Americans.

cards.title: Cesar Chavez
cards.description: Cesar Chavez fought for migrant farmworkers by organizing strikes and boycotts.

cards.title: Dolores Huerta
cards.description: Dolores Huerta co-founded the National Farm Workers Association with Cesar Chavez.

cards.title: The Feminist Movement
cards.description: The feminist movement of the 1960s and 70s sought equal rights and pay for women.

cards.title: The Feminine Mystique
cards.description: Betty Friedan’s book helped launch the modern women’s rights movement.

cards.title: Title IX
cards.description: Title IX (1972) banned sex discrimination in any education program receiving federal money.

cards.title: The American Indian Movement
cards.description: AIM was founded in 1968 to fight for Native American treaty rights and tribal sovereignty.

cards.title: The Occupation of Alcatraz
cards.description: Native American activists occupied the abandoned island prison for 19 months.

cards.title: The Stonewall Riots
cards.description: The 1969 Stonewall demonstrations in New York launched the modern LGBTQ+ rights movement.

cards.title: The Clean Air Act
cards.description: The Clean Air Act of 1970 was a major law to control and reduce air pollution.

cards.title: The EPA
cards.description: The Environmental Protection Agency was created in 1970 to protect health and the environment.

cards.title: Earth Day
cards.description: Earth Day was first celebrated on April 22, 1970, to raise awareness about protecting the planet.

cards.title: The Voting Age Lowered
cards.description: The 26th Amendment lowered the voting age from 21 to 18 during the Vietnam War era.

cards.title: The Counterculture
cards.description: The counterculture was a 1960s youth movement that rejected old norms and promoted peace.

cards.title: Woodstock
cards.description: The 1969 Woodstock festival was a three-day concert that became a symbol of the counterculture.

cards.title: The Assassination of MLK
cards.description: Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. was assassinated in Memphis in 1968, causing nationwide grief.

cards.title: Robert F. Kennedy
cards.description: Robert F. Kennedy, JFK’s brother and a presidential candidate, was also assassinated in 1968.

cards.title: The Warren Court
cards.description: The Warren Court, led by Chief Justice Earl Warren, was famous for expanding civil rights.

cards.title: The Vietnam War
cards.description: The Vietnam War was a long, divisive conflict to stop communist North Vietnam.

cards.title: The Domino Theory
cards.description: The Domino Theory said if one nation fell to communism, its neighbors would fall too.

cards.title: The Gulf of Tonkin Resolution
cards.description: This act let President Johnson greatly increase U.S. military involvement in Vietnam.

cards.title: Guerrilla Warfare
cards.description: The enemy in Vietnam used guerrilla warfare: surprise attacks and hidden traps.

cards.title: The Draft
cards.description: The draft was a system requiring young men to serve in the military during the Vietnam War.

cards.title: The Anti-War Movement
cards.description: Massive protests across campuses and cities called for an end to the Vietnam War.

cards.title: The Tet Offensive
cards.description: The 1968 Tet Offensive was a huge surprise attack that shook American confidence in the war.

cards.title: Apollo 11
cards.description: Apollo 11 landed the first humans on the Moon on July 20, 1969.

cards.title: Neil Armstrong
cards.description: Neil Armstrong was the first human to walk on the Moon.

cards.title: Buzz Aldrin
cards.description: Buzz Aldrin was the second human to walk on the Moon, alongside Neil Armstrong.

cards.title: President Richard Nixon
cards.description: Richard Nixon, the 37th President, ended U.S. involvement in Vietnam and opened relations with China.

cards.title: Vietnamization
cards.description: Vietnamization was Nixon’s policy of handing the fighting to the South Vietnamese army.

cards.title: The Paris Peace Accords
cards.description: The 1973 Paris Peace Accords officially ended direct U.S. military involvement in Vietnam.

cards.title: The Fall of Saigon
cards.description: In 1975, North Vietnam captured Saigon, uniting the country under communism.

cards.title: The Watergate Scandal
cards.description: Watergate was a scandal over a break-in at Democratic headquarters, covered up by President Nixon.

cards.title: Nixon’s Resignation
cards.description: In 1974, Richard Nixon became the first and only U.S. president to resign from office.

cards.title: President Gerald Ford
cards.description: Gerald Ford became the 38th President after Nixon resigned, and later pardoned him.

cards.title: The Bicentennial
cards.description: In 1976, the United States celebrated its 200th anniversary of independence.

cards.title: President Jimmy Carter
cards.description: Jimmy Carter, a former peanut farmer and Georgia governor, served as the 39th President.

cards.title: The Energy Crisis
cards.description: The 1970s energy crisis brought severe gas shortages and long lines at filling stations.

cards.title: The Camp David Accords
cards.description: In 1978, President Carter brokered a historic peace treaty between Egypt and Israel.

cards.title: The Iran Hostage Crisis
cards.description: American diplomats were held captive in Iran for 444 days after a revolution.

cards.title: Stagflation
cards.description: Stagflation was a 1970s problem where prices rose fast but the economy grew slowly.

cards.title: Three Mile Island
cards.description: A 1979 accident at a Pennsylvania nuclear plant raised fears about nuclear safety.

cards.title: The Rust Belt
cards.description: The "Rust Belt" describes Midwest manufacturing regions that declined as factories closed.

cards.title: President Ronald Reagan
cards.description: Ronald Reagan, the 40th President, was known for conservative policies and an optimistic style.

cards.title: Reaganomics
cards.description: Reaganomics focused on tax cuts, less government spending, and deregulation to spur business.

cards.title: Sandra Day O’Connor
cards.description: Appointed in 1981, Sandra Day O’Connor became the first woman on the U.S. Supreme Court.

cards.title: The Challenger Disaster
cards.description: In 1986, the space shuttle Challenger broke apart after takeoff, killing all seven astronauts.

cards.title: Christa McAuliffe
cards.description: Christa McAuliffe, a teacher set to be the first teacher in space, died in the Challenger disaster.

cards.title: The Personal Computer
cards.description: Computers made by companies like Apple and IBM became common in homes and offices in the 1980s.

cards.title: The Fall of the Berlin Wall
cards.description: In 1989, the Berlin Wall fell, signaling the collapse of communism in Europe.

cards.title: President George H.W. Bush
cards.description: George H.W. Bush, the 41st President, guided the U.S. through the end of the Cold War.

cards.title: The Gulf War
cards.description: In 1991, a U.S.-led coalition drove invading Iraqi forces out of Kuwait.

cards.title: Operation Desert Storm
cards.description: Operation Desert Storm was the official name for the combat phase of the Gulf War.

cards.title: The Collapse of the Soviet Union
cards.description: In 1991, the Soviet Union broke into 15 independent nations, ending the Cold War.

cards.title: The Internet
cards.description: Once a government project, the World Wide Web became public in the 1990s.

cards.title: President Bill Clinton
cards.description: Bill Clinton, the 42nd President, oversaw a period of strong economic prosperity in the 1990s.

cards.title: NAFTA
cards.description: NAFTA, the North American Free Trade Agreement, removed trade barriers between the U.S., Canada, and Mexico.

cards.title: The Dot-Com Boom
cards.description: The Dot-Com Boom was rapid growth in the late 1990s driven by internet companies.

cards.title: The Oklahoma City Bombing
cards.description: The 1995 Oklahoma City bombing was a domestic terrorist attack that killed 168 people.

cards.title: The Y2K Bug
cards.description: The Y2K bug was a widespread fear that computers would crash at the year 2000.

cards.title: The 2000 Election
cards.description: The 2000 presidential election was one of the closest ever, decided by a recount in Florida.

cards.title: President George W. Bush
cards.description: George W. Bush, the 43rd President, led the nation at the start of the War on Terror.

cards.title: The September 11 Attacks
cards.description: On September 11, 2001, terrorists hijacked four planes, attacking the World Trade Center and Pentagon.

cards.title: The War on Terror
cards.description: The War on Terror was an international military campaign launched after the September 11 attacks.

cards.title: The War in Afghanistan
cards.description: The U.S. invaded Afghanistan in 2001 to remove the Taliban regime sheltering those behind 9/11.

cards.title: The Department of Homeland Security
cards.description: A new cabinet department was created after 9/11 to protect the country from future attacks.

cards.title: The Iraq War
cards.description: The Iraq War began in 2003 when a U.S.-led coalition overthrew dictator Saddam Hussein.

cards.title: Hurricane Katrina
cards.description: In 2005, Hurricane Katrina caused historic flooding in New Orleans, Louisiana.

cards.title: The Smartphone Revolution
cards.description: The iPhone launched in 2007, changing how Americans communicate, work, and find information.

cards.title: The Great Recession
cards.description: The Great Recession of 2008 was a global downturn triggered by a collapse in the U.S. housing market.

cards.title: President Barack Obama
cards.description: Elected in 2008, Barack Obama made history as the first African American president.

cards.title: The Affordable Care Act
cards.description: The 2010 Affordable Care Act was a major reform to expand health insurance coverage.

cards.title: The Social Media Boom
cards.description: Platforms like Facebook, Twitter, and YouTube transformed culture and daily life in the 2010s.

cards.title: Deepwater Horizon
cards.description: The 2010 Deepwater Horizon disaster caused the largest marine oil spill in history.

cards.title: The Rise of SpaceX
cards.description: SpaceX, founded by Elon Musk, ushered in a new era of private commercial spaceflight.

cards.title: The Boston Marathon Bombing
cards.description: In 2013, a terrorist attack placed two bombs near the finish line of the Boston Marathon.

cards.title: Same-Sex Marriage
cards.description: In 2015, the Supreme Court ruled that same-sex marriage is legal in all 50 states.

cards.title: The Paris Climate Agreement
cards.description: The 2015 Paris Climate Agreement was a global pact to fight climate change.

cards.title: President Donald Trump
cards.description: Donald Trump, a businessman and TV personality, was elected the 45th President in 2016.

cards.title: The USMCA
cards.description: The 2018 USMCA was an updated trade deal between the U.S., Mexico, and Canada that replaced NAFTA.

cards.title: The COVID-19 Pandemic
cards.description: The 2020 COVID-19 pandemic caused lockdowns, remote school, and economic disruption.

cards.title: Operation Warp Speed
cards.description: Operation Warp Speed was a U.S. effort to speed up the development of COVID-19 vaccines.

cards.title: The Black Lives Matter Movement
cards.description: In 2020, nationwide protests called for racial justice and police reform after the death of George Floyd.

cards.title: The 2020 Census
cards.description: The 2020 Census found that the U.S. population had grown to over 331 million people.

cards.title: The January 6 Capitol Riot
cards.description: On January 6, 2021, protesters breached the U.S. Capitol during the electoral vote certification.

cards.title: President Joe Biden
cards.description: Joe Biden, formerly Obama’s vice president, was sworn in as the 46th President.

cards.title: Vice President Kamala Harris
cards.description: Kamala Harris became the first female, first African American, and first South Asian American Vice President.

cards.title: The End of the War in Afghanistan
cards.description: In 2021, the U.S. withdrew all military forces from Afghanistan, ending its longest war.

cards.title: The James Webb Space Telescope
cards.description: Launched in 2021, the James Webb telescope sends back the deepest images of the universe.

cards.title: Overturning Roe v. Wade
cards.description: In 2022, the Supreme Court ended federal constitutional protections for abortion, returning the issue to the states.

cards.title: The Rise of Artificial Intelligence
cards.description: Generative AI became a major focus of American innovation and daily life.

cards.title: Preparing for 250 Years
cards.description: The United States began preparing to celebrate its 250th anniversary of independence.

cards.title: E Pluribus Unum
cards.description: "E Pluribus Unum," the motto on American coins, means "Out of many, one."
